en.title: Jump Forward by Prime Steps
en.description:
Starting from index 0, you may only jump to a larger index j, where j−i must be prime and must not exceed nums[i]. Determine whether you can reach the last index. In the original example [2,3,1,1,0], you cannot jump 2 steps from index 2, so by the statement the output should be 0.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n maximum jump lengths; 1≤n≤200000, 0≤nums[i]≤10⁹.
en.explanation: Example 1: you can only go from 0 to 2, and nums[2]=1 cannot continue, so the correct answer is 0. Example 2: 1 is not prime, so no move is possible; output 0. Example 3: 0→2→4 uses two valid steps of 2, so output 1.
hints: Sieve the primes less than n and store them as a big-integer bitset. Represent pending positions as a bitset relative to the current index: take the prime bits up to the jump length and OR them in, then shift right to skip processed positions; avoid shifting the whole prime set left to absolute indices each time.
